$comment: MCP server scorecards, graded per scorecards/RUBRIC.md. Each entry describes the pinned commit only. Do not edit by hand without a grading pass.

clauderegistry-catalog.name: ClaudeRegistry Plugin Catalog

axes.title: Transport
axes.evidence: Single Streamable HTTP endpoint (src/index.js: StreamableHTTPServerTransport, sessionIdGenerator undefined); no HTTP+SSE surface.

axes.title: Stateless core
axes.evidence: A fresh McpServer per request; no session map. Module-level caches hold only shared public data (marketplace.json, verified.json) with last-good fallback.

axes.title: Lifecycle and protocol version
axes.evidence: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.x handles initialize/negotiation; the only declared capability (tools) is fully implemented (4 tools, all handlers live).

axes.title: Authorization
axes.evidence: Authless by design over read-only public catalog data, which the rubric permits only with abuse controls; those controls exist (per-IP rate limits, size caps, timeouts). No downstream token handling of any kind.

axes.title: Tool design
axes.evidence: Complete zod input/output schemas with per-field descriptions; honest annotations (catalog tools readOnlyHint, verify_plugin openWorldHint for its GitHub fetch); structured isError results; search output capped at 15 rows.

axes.title: Security hygiene
axes.evidence: Argument validation via zod plus regex allowlists (repo, ref, path); subprocess via execFileSync arg-arrays only (no shell); path-traversal rejection on inline files; 600KB body limit; 60s clone timeout and 25MB clone size guard; per-IP rate limits (30/h files, 10/h repo); no secrets in the repository; permissive CORS is appropriate for an authless read-only server.

notes: Rate-limit buckets are in-memory and therefore per-instance; adequate for the current single-instance deployment, but horizontal scaling would need a shared store.
No structured abuse logging or alerting yet; failures are visible only in pm2 logs.

History: v1.2.0 and earlier shipped no rate controls. That was tolerable while every tool served cached public JSON, but the verify_plugin tool (v1.3.0) makes the server do real work per call, and this grading pass forced the hardening before the tool launched.
